- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent prices are trending up.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days); apply a 1-2 day lag correction to avoid overreaction.
- If 3+ consecutive days of high sentiment + rising prices, model may overfit upward trend; cap forecast at 1.5x recent high unless sentiment shifts.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is 20%+ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5-10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period spikes (last 5-7 days); add 2-3% buffer if sentiment is bullish and price is trending up.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33 to 0.67) and price is volatile, model often misses short-term reversals; use 3-day moving average as sanity check.
